title: IBM is ending immigration sponsorship 'for the majority' of roles in its biggest unit
summary:
IBM said it's ending immigration sponsorships for "a majority of roles" in its biggest unit.
"IBM Consulting participates in U.S. high-skilled visa programs to address skill shortages," an IBM spokesperson said in a statement.
IBM Consulting is by far the largest unit of the tech giant.
In its 2025 annual report, IBM reported having 264,300 employees across IBM and its wholly owned subsidiaries.
The records are for IBM as a whole, meaning they alone wouldn't determine how many IBM Consulting employees are being sponsored.

title: Belgium Legalises Police Raids on Homes for Immigration Enforcement
summary:
Belgian lawmakers have approved legislation that will allow law enforcement to conduct early morning immigration raids to carry out deportations of foreign criminals and illegal migrants.
Previously, Minister for Asylum and Migration Anneleen Van Bossuyt of the governing New Flemish Alliance (N-VA), argued that the law was necessary to ensure that immigration enforcement could occur.
“Anyone residing here illegally who poses a threat to public order or national security must be able to be removed from the country,” Minister Van Bossuyt argued in July.
You are putting the safety of your own residents at risk,” Van Bossuyt said.
To that end, Minister Van Bossuyt was even deployed this week to the African nation of Cameroon to try to dissuade potential ill migrants from attempting to reach Belgium.

title: IBM’s biggest division ends most US foreign worker sponsorships
summary:
United States technology giant IBM has said it will stop sponsoring US foreign worker visas and green cards for most roles in its largest division.
A company spokesperson told Reuters on Tuesday that its consultancy unit had opted to end sponsorship for most roles.
IBM has become less reliant on so-called H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers in recent years.
The announcement comes as the Trump administration has increased pressure on major companies to cut down on their highly skilled foreign workforce in the US.
AdvertisementThe suspensions were announced within hours of Trump honouring Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.
